angle.title: Seeing the ad receipt is not the same as knowing the ads are working
angle.content_opportunity: Center the venue owner's practical situation: she could see the charges, but could not interpret performance or commit to weekly account checks. A fixed budget still needs oversight that fits someone's actual capacity. Use Whitney's lead-volume and cost walkthrough to support that ownership decision, rather than turning the Reel into a dashboard tutorial.
angle.strategic_rationale: Makes account oversight a manageable business responsibility rather than another demand on a busy owner. The commercial stake is whether an accepted level of spending remains worthwhile, not simply whether ads remain switched on.
angle.audience: Busy venue and wedding-business owners with running campaigns who want oversight without taking on daily account management.
angle.core_perspective: Knowing what you are spending does not tell you whether that spending still makes sense. There needs to be a realistic plan for who will review performance and recognize when it deserves a closer look.
angle.tension: The owner can accommodate the advertising expense without having the time or context to judge what it is buying.
angle.wia_expertise_in_action: Whitney separated spending limits from performance concerns, demonstrated lead and cost signals, and proposed scheduled specialist review. Kate supplied the capacity constraint that made a self-checking routine insufficient for her at that time.
angle.service_relevance: Illustrates account interpretation and the review support proposed in this call; it does not establish a currently available review package.
angle.reader_decision: Identify who will review campaign performance and which changes should prompt investigation, rather than relying on billing emails.
angle.selection_reason: The receipt-versus-understanding distinction gives familiar monitoring advice a concrete owner-facing consequence. It earns priority over the more familiar guided-DIY and foundations treatments.

angle.title: Reach couples who want the experience but have not considered your service
angle.content_opportunity: Use the ice-sculpture owner's expansion question: he reported strong visibility for his service and wanted to reach couples considering marquee lights or champagne towers without selling those services himself. Explore showing how the existing offer complements an experience couples already want. Keep Emily's complementary content and imagery as the concrete mechanism, with Whitney's buyer-readiness point in support.
angle.strategic_rationale: Addresses growth beyond existing service-name demand rather than assuming every advertising conversation begins with weak visibility. It makes buyer relevance and truthful offer boundaries the strategic issue, not a list of additional keywords or channels.
angle.audience: Specialist wedding suppliers who want to reach suitable couples before those couples search for their particular service.
angle.core_perspective: A specialist business does not have to add another service to broaden consideration. It can show how its existing offer contributes to an experience couples already want, while keeping what it actually sells clear.
angle.tension: Being visible to people already searching for a service leaves a different question: how does that service enter the consideration of people who have not thought of it yet?
angle.wia_expertise_in_action: Emily clarified the offer and developed the complementary-content and imagery recommendations. Whitney raised Pinterest alongside the blog strategy and explained why first-time awareness may need intermediate touchpoints before a detailed inquiry.
angle.reader_decision: Identify a relevant experience or adjacent interest through which to introduce the existing service, without implying that an unavailable service is for sale.
angle.selection_reason: The reported strength of core visibility and the owner's refusal to add another business create a substantive growth question. This adds a different thought to the oversight priority without relying on a success story.

angle.title: A tour-page view is not a booked tour
angle.content_opportunity: Build focused education around Whitney correcting her own description during the account walkthrough. Viewing the book-a-tour page, submitting an inquiry and booking a tour are different business steps. The useful question is what the conversion count actually records before an owner uses it to assess pipeline activity.
angle.strategic_rationale: Connects measurement precision to a recognizable venue decision: understanding whether advertising reports show website activity, inquiries or appointments. The live correction gives a familiar measurement lesson a specific commercial consequence.
angle.audience: Venue owners and wedding professionals interpreting conversion reports as evidence of inquiry or appointment activity.
angle.core_perspective: Judge a conversion count by the action it records. A visit to the tour page cannot tell an owner that a tour has been scheduled.
angle.tension: The name or description of a tracked action can suggest more progress toward a booking than the action establishes.
angle.wia_expertise_in_action: Whitney distinguished contact-page views from lead-form submissions and immediately corrected her description of the tour-page action before continuing the review.
angle.reader_decision: Check which action a reported conversion represents before treating the total as inquiries or booked appointments.
angle.selection_reason: A compact, supported business distinction makes this the reserve. Prefer it to a4 for a measurement Reel rather than keeping two tracking explainers in the recommendation set.

angle.inference: An aggregate conversion total should not be assumed to represent one commercial outcome.
